newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Sao Paulo bolsa sees lower foreign inflows in June.
newsitem.headline: Sao Paulo bolsa sees lower foreign inflows in June.

text.p: Net foreign capital inflows into the Sao Paulo Stock Exchange (Bovespa) dropped sharply in June to 22.186 million reais, down from 259.295 million reais in the previous month, the bolsa said.
Foreign trading, however, increased significantly last month, it said.

Foreign buys totalled 6.054 billion reais, up 53.4 percent from 3.944 billion reais in May. Sales from foreign investors amounted to 6.076 billion reais, against 3.685 billion reais in the previous month.

The bolsa's figures showed that foreign investors opted to take profits at the end of the first half, traders said. The data also confirm that domestic equity funds and investors were the primary force behind the bolsa's 10.7-percent rise in June, they added.
So far this year, net foreign investment in the Sao Paulo bourse has totalled 1.448 billion reais, it added.
